PROJECT NO. 55999

REPORTS OF THE ELECTRIC PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
RELABILITY COUNCIL OF TEXAS OF TEXAS

## ELECTRIC RELIABILITY COUNCIL OF TEXAS, INC.’S NOTICE OF RELIABILITY ANALYSIS DETERMINATION AND REQUEST FOR GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTION

Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) provides this notification to the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) of the results of ERCOT’s reliability analysis of the proposed retirement of three Generation Resources in March 2025 and requests a good cause exception to vary from the timeline set forth in the ERCOT Protocols addressing the processes for potentially entering into one or more agreements for Reliability Must-Run (RMR) or Must-Run Alternative (MRA) service.

## I. Results of Reliability Analysis

On March 13, 2024, ERCOT received Parts I and II of Notifications of Suspension of Operations (NSOs) from CPS Energy regarding the planned retirement of three Generation Resources on March 31, 2025. The three Generation Resources and their summer Seasonal Net Maximum Sustainable Ratings are provided below.

• BRAUNIG_VHB1 (217 MW)
• BRAUNIG_VHB2 (230 MW)
• BRAUNIG_VHB3 (412 MW)

Hereinafter, these Generation Resources are referred to as “the Braunig Resources.”

Under paragraph (1) of ERCOT Protocols § 3.14.1.2, ERCOT followed the processes for providing notice and opportunity for comment on the NSOs for the Braunig Resources.<sup>1</sup> As required under PUC rule 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.502(e) and ERCOT Protocols

<sup>1</sup> See ERCOT Market Notice. M-C031324-01 Notifications of Suspension of Operations (NSOs) for CPS Energy (BRAUNIG VIIB1, BRAUNIG VIIB2, BRAUNIG VIIB3), March 13, 2024, available at https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/nikt_notices/M-C031324-01.

---

§ 3.14.1.2, ERCOT also timely conducted its reliability analysis of whether the Braunig Resources would be needed to support ERCOT System reliability.<sup>2</sup>

Yesterday, on April 22, 2024, ERCOT issued a public Market Notice on the results of its reliability analysis. ERCOT’s analysis identified ERCOT System performance deficiencies that are materially impacted by the retirement of the Braunig Resources. In summary, without the Braunig Resources, there were transmission facilities loaded above their normal rating under pre-contingency conditions for which the Braunig Resources had an unloading Shift Factor of more than 2% and an unloading impact of more than 5%, transmission facilities that were above 110% emergency loading for which the Braunig Resources had an unloading Shift Factor of more than 2% and an unloading impact of more than 5%, and cascading under studied conditions identified in paragraph (3)(c)(ii) of ERCOT Protocols § 3.14.1.2. Therefore, the Braunig Resources are needed to support ERCOT System reliability. ERCOT has posted the report on its reliability analysis to ERCOT’s Market Information System (MIS) Secure Area.<sup>3</sup>

## II. Request for Good Cause Exception

The Commission’s rule that addresses the RMR and MRA processes, 16 TAC § 25.502, contemplates that by the proposed retirement date of March 31, 2025, ERCOT will 1) enter into an RMR agreement, 2) enter into one or more MRA agreements, or 3) determine that the Braunig Resources are needed for reliability, but are not a cost-effective solution to the identified reliability concern.<sup>4</sup> ERCOT fully intends to meet this timeline.

The ERCOT Protocols, however, provide a more prescriptive—and in this case faster—timeline for ERCOT to complete the MRA and RMR processes. Paragraph (6) of ERCOT Protocols § 3.14.1.2 requires ERCOT to issue the MRA RFP within 10 days of determining the retirement of the Braunig Resources would result in performance deficiencies and set an RFP schedule that permits response evaluation within 150 days of CPS Energy’s submission of the

<sup>2</sup> Paragraph (3)(c) of ERCOT Protocols § 3.14.1.2 sets forth the criteria for ERCOT’s reliability analysis. Under the 16 TAC § 25.502(c) and ERCOT Protocols § 3.14.1.2(5), ERCOT must complete its reliability analysis within 60 calendar days of receiving Parts I and II of an NSO. Thus, the deadline for completing the reliability analysis on the Braunig Resources is Sunday, May 12, 2024.

<sup>3</sup> Because the report includes engineering or vulnerability information that could pose a security risk, an ERCOT Digital Certificate is required to access the MIS Secure Area.

<sup>4</sup> 16 T.A.C. 25.502(e).

---

NSO. Respectively, those deadlines would be Thursday, May 2, 2024 for MRA RFP issuance and Saturday, August 10, 2024 for response evaluation.

Regarding a potential RMR agreement, under paragraph (7) of ERCOT Protocols §3.14.1.2, CPS Energy must submit an initial estimated budget and Part III of the NSO, providing an estimated RMR fuel adder and a proposed initial standby cost for RMR service, within 10 days of ERCOT determining the retirement of the Braunig Resources would result in performance deficiencies. Within 11 days of the determination, ERCOT must begin good faith negotiations with CPS Energy for an RMR agreement. Respectively, those deadlines would be Thursday, May 2, 2024 and Friday, May 3, 2024.

However, ERCOT has determined that it will not be able to comply with its RMR and MRA deadlines in the ERCOT Protocols. Due to resource constraints, ERCOT cannot simultaneously devote resources to the RMR and MRA processes while also devoting the same resources to addressing potential mitigation mechanisms to address the South Texas Export Generic Transmission Constraints this summer.<sup>5</sup> For this reason, ERCOT seeks a good cause exception, under 16 TAC §25.3(b), from the RMR and MRA deadlines in the ERCOT Protocols.

Granting this exception would also serve the public interest. The deadlines for the RMR and MRA processes in the ERCOT Protocols were established to permit sufficient time for completion of these activities in the event of a Resource Entity providing the minimum, 150-day prescribed notice for an NSO. Here, CPS Energy has provided more than a year of advanced notice. Granting an exception to the RMR and MRA deadlines will give ERCOT more than sufficient time to meet the timeline contemplated in the PUC’s rule, and conducting the MRA and RMR processes closer to the proposed retirement date will result in more accurate information (including operations and pricing data from this summer) regarding the value of any RMR or MRA service that might begin next spring. Delay of the MRA RFP could also avoid the potential confusion of having two pending RFPs, addressing two different services and time frames (specifically, a possible capacity service for this summer under a contract for capacity and MRA service beginning in 2025).

Because the Commission’s direction on the summer 2024 contract for capacity will be the most significant factor in determining when ERCOT will be able to begin development of the

<sup>5</sup> See ERCOT’s Update Regarding South Texas Export Constraint Mitigation Solutions (Apr. 22, 2024) for discussion of this work.

---

MRA RFP, ERCOT would intend to propose a timeline for the MRA RFP and other MRA- and RMR-related processes once a decision has been made on whether to pursue a summer 2024 contract for capacity. Any proposed timeline will ensure sufficient time for developing and evaluating responses to the RFP and comparing these to an RMR commitment of the Braunig Resources.

ERCOT conferred with CPS Energy regarding its intention to seek this good cause exception and is authorized to represent that CPS Energy does not oppose the request.

ERCOT respectfully attaches a draft Proposed Order for the Commission’s consideration. ERCOT appreciates the Commission’s consideration of this request. ERCOT would be pleased to provide any additional information and will attend the Commission’s April 25 and May 2 open meetings to address Commissioner comments or questions.

Respectfully submitted,

## REPORTS OF THE ELECTRIC PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
RELABILITY COUNCIL OF TEXAS OF TEXAS

## DRAFT PROPOSED ORDER GRANTING GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTION

On March 13, 2024, CPS Energy submitted to the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) Parts I and II of Notifications of Suspension of Operations (NSOs) regarding CPS Energy’s planned retirement of three Generation Resources, BRAUNIG_VHB1, BRAUNIG_VHB2, and BRAUNIG_VHB3. CPS Energy proposes to retire these Generation Resources on March 31, 2025.

On April 22, 2024, ERCOT issued a public Market Notice on the results of ERCOT’s reliability analysis in which ERCOT identified ERCOT System performance deficiencies that are materially impacted by the retirement of the three Generation Resources.

On April 23, 2024, ERCOT filed with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) a request for a good cause exception, under 16 TAC § 25.3(b), from the deadlines in the ERCOT Protocols associated with entering into an agreement for a Reliability Must-Run (RMR) service with CPS Energy or Must-Run Alternative (MRA) service with an alternative provider, both related to the planned retirement of the three Generation Resources.

The Commission grants ERCOT’s request for a good cause exception due to its resource constraints and to provide more timely data for evaluating any potential RMR or MRA service. ERCOT must notify the Commission once it has determined an appropriate timeline for these activities.
